words.engDef: an expert estimate of quality, performance, or value
words.example: The human resources manager conducted annual performance appraisals this week.

words.engDef: to repay a person who has spent money on business expenses
words.example: The firm will reimburse you for all travel and lodging expenses.

words.engDef: the action of repaying someone for spent business expenses
words.example: Please submit your receipts to the accounting office for reimbursement.

words.engDef: a process of testing the ability, character, or suitability of a worker
words.example: New employees must complete a three-month probation period before receiving benefits.

words.engDef: relating to a period of probation or testing of an employee
words.example: During the probationary period, her work will be closely monitored by her supervisor.

words.engDef: pay or benefits received when employment is terminated
words.example: The laid-off engineers received a severance package equivalent to six months of pay.

words.engDef: documents or qualifications proving a person's suitability for a job
words.example: The candidate has outstanding academic credentials and extensive practical experience.

words.engDef: paid for services or work performed
words.example: This is a highly demanding but very handsomely remunerated position.

words.engDef: money paid for work or a service; compensation
words.example: The company offers competitive remuneration packages to attract top talent.

words.engDef: a recruiter who identifies and approaches suitable candidates for senior positions
words.example: A professional headhunter contacted him regarding a director position at a competitor firm.

words.engDef: the gradual reduction of a workforce by employees leaving and not being replaced
words.example: Instead of firing staff, the company is reducing its size through natural attrition.

words.engDef: the rate at which employees leave a workforce and are replaced; or revenue
words.example: High employee turnover can be extremely costly for a modern business.

words.engDef: an extra benefit supplementing salary, such as health insurance or a company car
words.example: Our company offers excellent fringe benefits, including dental care and a free gym membership.

words.engDef: casual term for fringe benefits or special privileges
words.example: Free snacks and flexible working hours are some of the perks of working at a tech startup.

words.chinese: 員工薪資名冊，薪資總額
words.engDef: a list of employees and the amount of money they are paid
words.example: The accounting office is responsible for processing the monthly payroll.

words.engDef: a temporary or permanent discharge of workers due to economic conditions
words.example: The factory announced the layoff of two hundred temporary assembly line workers.

words.chinese: （為被裁員工提供的）轉職就業協助
words.engDef: the provision of assistance to laid-off employees in finding new jobs
words.example: As part of the severance package, the firm provided outplacement services to the staff.

words.chinese: 候選人複選名冊；列入複選名單
words.engDef: a list of selected candidates from which a final choice is made
words.example: The hiring committee has shortlisted three applicants for the final interview.

words.engDef: the process of investigating someone's background before hiring them
words.example: A thorough vetting process is mandatory for all high-level security positions.

words.engDef: the process or action of introducing someone to a new job or office
words.example: The human resources department organized a comprehensive induction program for new hires.

words.engDef: a fixed regular sum of money paid as a salary or allowance
words.example: The university provides a modest monthly stipend to graduate research assistants.

words.engDef: a payment given for professional services rendered nominally without charge
words.example: The guest speaker received an honorarium of five hundred dollars for her lecture.

words.engDef: a fee paid in advance to secure professional services, especially an attorney
words.example: The legal consultant requires a monthly retainer to handle our corporate accounts.

words.engDef: a person whose job is to enlist or hire new employees
words.example: The corporate recruiter screened hundreds of resumes for the marketing vacancy.

words.engDef: a person who assesses the value of property or the quality of performance
words.example: The bank sent an independent appraiser to assess the market value of the office building.
